title: The Biggest Stomp-Print Ever

topics.value_lesson: Trying again when something wobbles and falls — each rebuild makes it stronger

spine: A storyteller remembers the day the dinosaurs built a giant mud footprint together, wobble by wobble, until it was big enough to sit in and ROAR about.

child_name.role: the child listening, who in the memory was there helping

segments.text: I remember a morning on the sandy riverbank, where the mud was soft and the ferns waved tall. Grandpa Ankylosaurus thumped his tail club. Boom. Boom. "Today," he said, "we build the BIGGEST stomp-print ever! A stomp you can keep! So big {child_name} can sit inside it!" So we gathered. Stegosaurus carried pebbles on her plates. Plop, plop. A little feathered dinosaur fluttered down with fluff in her beak. "Oooh," she said, "what does THAT do?" We patted the mud flat, flat, flat. Soft as porridge. But nobody knew how to make the three toes yet — and the toes are the whole footprint.

"Stomp it is!" says Baby Triceratops. Up, up she rears — and STOMP! STOMP! STOMP! Three big toes! Mud goes splash! "Again! Again!" we shout, and she giggles so hard her horns wobble. But then — bloop. One toe wall slides down, slow as honey. The little feathered dinosaur flutters close and peeks in. "Oooh," she says, "why did it fall?" Grandpa's eyes go twinkly. "A wobble is a teacher!" he booms. And we look at the slumpy toe, and we start to think.

"Slow and gentle," says Stegosaurus, and she tips her sunny plates. Plop, plop, plop — three smooth pebbles for three toes. We pat-pat-pat, one little push at a time. So neat! So tidy! But the little feathered dinosaur tilts her head. "Oooh," she says, "is that a toe for a mouse?" We look. The middle toe is teeny-tiny — more a dimple than a toe. Grandpa's eyes go twinkly. "A wobble is a teacher!" he booms. And we look at the little toe, and we start to think.

Grandpa Ankylosaurus nodded at the mud. "First we pat. Flat, flat, flat." Boom, boom, boom went his tail club. We patted too, with our hands and our feet. Then we pressed the three toes in, slow and careful. Baby Triceratops bumped the wall with her frill. Bump! It stayed! Stegosaurus plopped pebbles on for toenails. Plop, plop. The little feathered dinosaur tucked fluff into the cracks. "Oooh," she said, "what did YOU find?" We stepped back. A stomp-print as long as a bathtub! Big enough to sit in! Grandpa lifted his head. "Now — how do we CELEBRATE a footprint this fine?"

"We ROAR!" said Grandpa. So we lined up all around the print. "One, two — ROOOAR!" we shouted. ROOOAR went the dinosaurs. Roar! went {child_name}. One roar is fun. Everyone roaring is a whole song! Then one stomp each. Stomp! Stomp! STOMP! Up burst the birds from the ferns — flutter, flutter, like confetti in the sky! The little feathered dinosaur spun in a circle. "Oooh! It tickles my FEATHERS!" Grandpa pressed one smooth pebble into my hand, warm from the sun. A pebble toenail, just for me. And that pebble sits on my shelf still.

"We SIT!" said Grandpa. So I climbed down, down, into the stomp-print. Squish went the mud. I sat right inside it, small as an egg in a nest. "It is SO big," I said. "It is SO you-sized," said Grandpa. The little feathered dinosaur fluttered down and tucked one soft feather behind my ear. "Oooh," she said, "what does THAT do?" A small bird landed on the edge. Tweet-tweet! it sang. And she sang back — tweet-tweet! — almost the same. Then home we went, squish, squash, squish. And that feather is in my pocket still, soft as the day it was given.

gathered_but_unused: Some dinosaurs were as tall as a house, with legs like tree trunks that went thump thump thump when they walked.
Brachiosaurus had a neck so long it could nibble leaves at the very top of tall trees, like a living ladder.
Dinosaurs hatched from eggs, and some nests had eggs as big as footballs.
Stegosaurus had big flat plates standing up all along its back, like a row of kites.
Ankylosaurus had a big bony club on the end of its tail and a lumpy armored back, like wearing a shell.
Triceratops had three horns on its face and a big frill on its neck, like wearing a fancy collar.
Tyrannosaurus rex had feet so big that one footprint could be as long as a bathtub, and its roar was very, very loud.
Many scientists think some dinosaurs had feathers, soft and fluffy like a baby chick.
